description: Train a neural network to approximate the map from Taylor coefficients (a_2,...,a_N) of univalent functions to their Bloch radius B_f. This surrogate model enables rapid exploration of the coefficient space. Combined with adversarial training, this could discover near-extremal functions.
mathematical_formalization: Define Φ(a_2,...,a_N) = B_{f_N}. Train NN: Φ̂(a;θ) ≈ Φ(a). Then B_u ≈ inf_{a ∈ U_N} Φ̂(a;θ) where U_N = {a : f_N univalent}.
implementation_hypothesis: Sample 100K random univalent functions (de Branges coefficients). For each, compute B_f numerically. Train ResNet on (a_2,...,a_20) → B_f. Use gradient descent to find minimum.
experiment_seed: Generate 50000 random univalent polynomials of degree 15. Compute B_f via numerical conformal mapping. Train 4-layer MLP.
